subtopic: Magnetic Effect of Current — Conductor, Loop and Solenoid
stem:
Two long parallel conductors I and II placed at right angles to a metre scale, at the 2 cm and 6 cm marks, as shown. They carry currents of 1 A and 3 A respectively in the same direction. They will produce zero magnetic field at the

(The figure shows a horizontal centimetre scale marked 0 to 13 cm. Conductor I is at the 2 cm mark and conductor II is at the 6 cm mark, both perpendicular to the scale, carrying currents in the same direction.)

options.label: A
options.text: 6 cm mark

options.label: B
options.text: 3 cm mark

options.label: C
options.text: zero mark

options.label: D
options.text: 10 cm mark

subtopic: Magnetic Effect of Current — Conductor, Loop and Solenoid
stem: The graph showing the variation of the magnetic field strength (B) with distance (r) from a long current carrying conductor is

options.label: A
options.text: a straight line through the origin: B increases linearly (in direct proportion) with r

options.label: B
options.text: an upward-curving line: B increases more and more steeply as r increases

options.label: C
options.text: a concave decreasing curve: B starts high and falls towards zero as r increases

options.label: D
options.text: a rectangular hyperbola: B falls steeply at first then levels off, i.e. B is inversely proportional to r

subtopic: Magnetic Effect of Current — Conductor, Loop and Solenoid
stem:
A wire is placed perpendicular to the plane through point O. A constant current is flowing in the wire out of the plane. In the figure, the two points where the magnetic field will be perpendicular to each other is

(The figure shows two perpendicular lines crossing at O in the plane of the paper: U is directly above O, V is directly below O, X is to the left of O and Y is to the right of O. The wire pierces the plane at O carrying current out of the page, so the field circles around O and at each point is tangent to the circle through it.)

options.label: A
options.text: V and Y

options.label: B
options.text: U and V

options.label: C
options.text: X and V

options.label: D
options.text: X and Y

subtopic: Force on a Current-Carrying Conductor and Electric Motor
stem:
A rectangular loop ABCD carrying a current I is situated near a straight conductor XY, such that the conductor is parallel to the side AB of the loop and is in the plane of the loop. If a steady current I is established in the conductor XY, the loop will

(The figure shows a long straight conductor XY on the left and, to its right, a rectangular loop ABCD; the side AB of the loop is parallel to and nearest the conductor XY, both carrying current in the same direction.)

options.label: A
options.text: move towards the side AB of the loop

options.label: B
options.text: remain stationary

options.label: C
options.text: rotate about its axis

options.label: D
options.text: move away from the side AB of the loop

subtopic: Magnetic Effect of Current — Conductor, Loop and Solenoid
stem: The pattern of the magnetic field produced inside a current carrying solenoid is

options.label: A
options.text: curved lines that diverge and loop around, like the field of a bar magnet seen near a single turn

options.label: B
options.text: lines that are nearly straight in the middle but bulge out and loop around at the two ends (the field of the whole solenoid)

options.label: C
options.text: concentric circles around a central point (the field around a single straight wire)

options.label: D
options.text: uniform, straight, equally-spaced parallel lines all pointing the same way

subtopic: Magnetic Effect of Current — Conductor, Loop and Solenoid
stem:
An electric current passes through a straight wire. If magnetic compasses are placed at the points X and Y as shown, then

(The figure shows a horizontal straight wire carrying current I towards the right. A compass needle is placed at point X just above the wire and another at point Y just below the wire.)

options.label: A
options.text: the needles will deflect in the same direction

options.label: B
options.text: only one of the needles will deflect

options.label: C
options.text: the needles will not deflect

options.label: D
options.text: the needles will deflect in the opposite directions

subtopic: Force on a Current-Carrying Conductor and Electric Motor
stem:
A wire is placed between the magnetic poles as shown in figure. In which direction does a force act on the wire?

(The figure shows a horseshoe-type arrangement with the N pole on the left and the S pole on the right, so the magnetic field between the poles points horizontally from N to S. A straight wire passes vertically between the poles, carrying current vertically upward.)

options.label: A
options.text: Vertically upward on the wire

options.label: B
options.text: From west to east

options.label: C
options.text: Vertically downward on the wire

options.label: D
options.text: From east to west

subtopic: Force on a Current-Carrying Conductor and Electric Motor
stem:
A straight wire is placed between two poles of a magnet as shown in figure. If an alternating current is passing through the wire, then the wire will

(The figure shows the N pole on the left and the S pole on the right, with a vertical conducting wire passing between them in the plane of the poles; the field points horizontally from N to S.)

options.label: A
options.text: Move out of the page only

options.label: B
options.text: Move out and into the page

options.label: C
options.text: Move into the page only

options.label: D
options.text: Remain stationary

subtopic: Force on a Current-Carrying Conductor and Electric Motor
stem:
A uniform magnetic field exists in the plane of paper as shown in the diagram. In this field, an electron (e⁻) and a positron (p⁺) enter as shown. The electron and positron experience force

(The figure shows horizontal magnetic field lines pointing to the right in the plane of the paper. An electron e⁻ on the left moves vertically downward along its path, while a positron p⁺ on the right moves vertically upward along its path.)

options.label: A
options.text: pointing out of the plane of the paper and into the plane of the paper respectively

options.label: B
options.text: both pointing out of the plane of the paper

options.label: C
options.text: pointing into the plane of the paper and out of the plane of the paper respectively

options.label: D
options.text: both pointing into the plane of the paper
